In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PNP(tBU) pincer ligands can be considered as non-innocent, and this is manifested by the fact that the ligand can act as a one-electron donor to the metal center.
the Ni(II) PNP(tBu)-complexes show a remarkable versatility in terms of ligand substitution and coordination chemistry.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PNP ligand can be used as a non-innocence ligand for the synthesis and characterization of Ni(II)-alkyl and thiolato complexes.
the PNP(tBU) pincer ligands can easily be protonated or deprotonated and the Ni(II) center is able to accommodate the resulting changes in formal oxidation state of the PNP ligand.
the PNP(tBi) ligand is a versatile ligand for the synthesis of Ni(II) compounds with a variety of different oxidation states and coordination geometries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PNP(tBi) ligand can be easily tuned to form a variety of Ni(II) compounds, and that the ligand is non-innocent and can be reversibly dearomatized.
the PNP(tBi) ligand can be used as a non-innocently coordinating ligand to stabilize both neutral and dicationic Ni(II)-thiolate species, and the ligand is able to stabilize a Ni(II)-alkyl species.
the PNP(t Bu) backbone is a versatile platform that can accommodate various ligands, and that the ligand can be reversibly dearomatized and reprotonated.
